claims.content: The Auctioneer wants to schedule a new auction event by selecting products, applying them to the event, and setting the timeframe and parameters such as date range, product type, cost range, and duration.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Auctioneer schedules a new auction event by selecting products, applying them to the event, and setting the event's timeframe and parameters (date range, product type, cost range, duration).
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Auctioneer schedules one auction event: selects the product list, applies it to the event, and sets the date range and duration; the event is scheduled with the chosen product and parameters.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Auctioneer begins scheduling a new auction event.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The auction event is scheduled with selected product and configured parameters (date range, product type, cost range, duration).
in_scope_actions: Selecting product for the auction event
Applying selected product to the event
Setting parameters: product type, cost range, duration
excluded_adjacent_actions: Publishing the planned event schedule to site visitors and bidders
Viewing or editing existing current/scheduled auctions as a separate management activity
Editing selected auction items after searching/selecting a product list

claims.content: Auctioneer
The Auctioneer is authenticated and logged into the system.
The Auctioneer is in the Auction Administration module configured for viewing/editing current or scheduled auctions.
The system's scheduling window extends at least one month into the future so the auction event's date range can be scheduled.
Products available to the Auctioneer for selection have an available image and are in a valid, sellable inventory location.
The Auctioneer triggers the use case by selecting the 'Create New Auctions' option from the Administration Menu / Auction Admin Main Menu (or accessing the 'Create New Auctions Page').
The Auctioneer uses the Search Section to locate candidate products by entering or selecting search criteria such as Product ID, Cost Range, and Product Type.
The system displays the matching products in a search-results grid with an Action column and product information including Product ID, Description, Cost, and Product Type.
The Auctioneer selects the products to include in the auction event using the checkboxes in the Action column, optionally using 'Choose All'.
The Auctioneer applies the selected products to the event by choosing the 'Create grouping / event' operation from the Action list.
The Auctioneer sets the event's date range and duration by choosing a standard auction duration or manually selecting starting and ending dates/times.
The Auctioneer clicks 'Create New Auction' to create the auction event containing all selected products with the configured date range and duration.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of manually setting the event's date range and duration, the Auctioneer may apply a pre-defined event profile to all selected items by selecting one profile from a list box and clicking the 'Apply' button; the profile configures the event parameters.
Diverges from Step 5: When applying ending/starting times to all selected items, the Auctioneer must choose the specific time from a dropdown list located in the column header.

Diverges from Step 6: If the Auctioneer attempts to create the auction with the same starting and ending date/time, the system displays an error message and highlights (color-codes) the offending data.

Diverges from Step 6: Before the auction is created, if any item being scheduled has additional quantities of the same item already scheduled in overlapping auction events, the system displays a popup warning to the Auctioneer.

At main flow Step 6, if the Auctioneer attempts to create the auction with identical starting and ending date/time, the system displays an error message and highlights (color-codes) the offending data; no auction event is created, and the use case returns to Step 5 so the Auctioneer can correct the date range/duration.

Before the auction is created at main flow Step 6, if any item being scheduled has additional quantities of the same item already scheduled in overlapping auction events, the system displays a popup warning; after the Auctioneer acknowledges the warning, the use case returns to Step 6 to continue creation.

At main flow Step 5, while configuring parameters via the event-profile alternative, if the Auctioneer applies a profile restricted to a specific category (e.g., 'Apply to Gemstones Only') to a grouping of items outside that category, the system generates an error message stating the profile can only be applied to products in the specified category; the operation is prevented and the use case remains at Step 5 to select a valid profile.
The system creates an auction event containing all selected items, with each item's applied and/or manually input data parameters.
The selected products are shown in the search results grid with updated 'Starts' and 'Ends' timestamps corresponding to the newly scheduled auction event.
The 'Duration' column for each selected item is updated to reflect the configured length of the new auction event (e.g., '1-Hour', '2-Day').
